newsitem.title: USA: US High Court sides with Exxon on gas tax.
newsitem.headline: US High Court sides with Exxon on gas tax.

text.p: The U.S. Supreme Court Monday sided with Exxon Corp in a case on the application of the depletion allowance for natural gas producers, an issue the federal government says affects more than $1 billion in taxes for the company over several years.
At issue was a section of the Internal Revenue tax code that authorizes a depletion deduction for oil and gas producers equal to 22 percent of the producer's gross income from the property.

The Internal Revenue Service determined that Exxon was not allowed to use a representative market or field price in calculating its depletion deduction when that price exceeded the actual gross income it received from its sales of the gas.
The dispute involved long-term natural gas contracts Exxon entered into from 1953 through 1972 on oil and gas wells in eastern Texas and along the Texas Gulf Coast.

The U.S. Justice Department in appealing to the Supreme Court said Exxon has raised the issue "in a series of lawsuits and audits that involve several different tax years. The taxes at issue in these several years exceed $1 billion."
But the high court sided with Exxon and denied the government appeal without any comment or dissent, letting stand a U.S. appeals court ruling in the company's favor.
